title: Riddle Granny Disappearance Case
notes: Recurring detective-cast convention follows ep011: Conan Edogawa is omitted (his few analytical lines are not clearly speaker-attributed in this un-tagged transcript and he plays the same background-catalyst role as in other episodes). Ayumi Yoshida, Mitsuhiko Tsuburaya and Genta Kojima are NOT on that omit list and are kept as full person nodes with roles=[witness]: they are the ones entrusted with the victim's belongings, the ones who discover the bloody coded scarf, and the ones who solve the kanji cipher on-screen, so they are load-bearing to the plot the way Ran/Kogoro are not in ep011. No event nodes: actions are direct typed edges. This transcript carries no speaker-name tags (unlike some other episodes' (Character Card) markup), so a few group-scene was_at attributions (e.g. exactly who accompanied Ayumi to Ezaki's house) are inferred from narrative context rather than an explicit speaker label; this is flagged here rather than silently presented as certain. IMPORTANT DISCREPANCY vs. the old wiki-derived cases/ep273 file: that file modeled ONLY the one-month-earlier backstory murder of Ezaki (as e1) and a vague kidnapping (e2) with a single generic victim (Mr. Ezaki) and two bare-name suspects, and it never created a node for Shizuka Oomori at all -- despite her disappearance/kidnapping being the entire on-screen 'case' the episode's title refers to (the 'Granny' of 'Riddle Granny Disappearance Case'). The old file also omitted the coded-scarf kanji puzzle (the actual detective mechanism used to solve the case), the specific identification of the murder weapon (the white-eyed monkey statue out of the three-wise-monkeys ornament set), and Joji Yabuki's on-screen red-herring confrontation/clearance arc. The culprit identity (Toshio Mochizuki) matches the old file and the transcript -- label.murderer_id is unchanged -- but the surrounding graph in the old file was missing most of the actual case. case_type: murder + kidnapping/false imprisonment.

locations.name: Storage locker facility near Koshin Tower / Koshin Street shopping district

attrs.significance: where Shizuka was confined inside a disused locker; Mochizuki had arranged for the lockers to be 'transferred' (discarded) at 2 o'clock

attrs.composition: Mizaru (see no evil), Iwazaru (speak no evil), and Kikazaru (hear no evil) -- the three wise monkeys, plus other ape figurines
attrs.provenance: belonged to Ezaki; inherited by Mochizuki after Ezaki's death

attrs.identifying_feature: eyes painted white, distinguishing it from the other monkey statues -- specified in Shizuka's coded message
attrs.forensic_result: bloodstains on it matched Ezaki, confirmed after Shizuka's rescue and testimony

attrs.found_on: tied around the neck of the stray cat Bruce
attrs.cipher: eight instances of the kanji 'hi' (day, 日), each altered by one added stroke into a different character: me (eye, 目), shiro (white, 白), ta (rice field, 田), kyu (former, 旧), yoshi (reason/motive, 由), kou (甲), tan/dan (dawn -- also read as in 'danna', husband, 旦), shin (monkey, 申)
attrs.decoded_message: Her 'former husband' (Ezaki) was murdered -- silenced (the 'ta' character read as mouth shut by an X). The motive/reason points to the Koshin (three-wise-monkeys) ornament set, and the specific weapon is the white-eyed monkey statue among them.
attrs.decoding_method: solved collaboratively by the Detective Boys as a kanji stroke-addition puzzle, the same style of quiz Shizuka used to give Ayumi about the cats

attrs.cover_story: Mochizuki told facility staff it held only old junk and could be thrown away
attrs.schedule: arranged to be carried off/discarded at 2 o'clock the day Shizuka was found

attrs.significance: carried Shizuka's bloodstained coded scarf out of captivity, alerting the Detective Boys and giving them the clue that broke the case; later, by meowing from inside a car engine, startled off a thief trying to steal Yabuki's car
